root_cause: pool2's pods run in the new subnet snet-aks-pool2 (10.240.2.0/24), but the sql-ledger server's virtual network rules cover only snet-aks-pool1 (rule allow-snet-aks-pool1) and snet-aks-pool2 has no Microsoft.Sql service endpoint, so connections from pool2 pod IPs such as 10.240.2.15 are rejected by the server's access controls with error 40615 while pool1 pods still connect.
evidence: az-aks-nodepool-list.json: pool2's vnetSubnetId points to snet-aks-pool2 while nodepool1 uses snet-aks-pool1
az-sql-server-vnet-rule-list.json: the sql-ledger server has exactly one virtual network rule, allow-snet-aks-pool1, covering only the pool1 subnet
az-network-vnet-subnet-show-pool2.json: snet-aks-pool2 has an empty serviceEndpoints list — no Microsoft.Sql service endpoint (red herring checked: the attached nsg-aks-spoke allows outbound 1433)
app.log: 40615 'Client with IP address 10.240.2.15 is not allowed to access the server' — a pool2 pod IP, blocked by the server's vnet rules despite the NSG being permissive
kubectl-get-pods-wide.txt: pool2 pods Running at 10.240.2.x addresses with connection-failure restarts; pool1 pods at 10.240.1.x are stable — the pods themselves are healthy
fix: Give the pool2 subnet access to the sql-ledger server: add a virtual network rule for snet-aks-pool2 on the sql-ledger server (requires the Microsoft.Sql service endpoint on the subnet, which az-network-vnet-subnet-show-pool2.json shows is missing — enable it first), or move the database behind a private endpoint reachable from the whole vnet-aks-spoke.
